description: Build and maintain a design system from component audit through token definition, component library creation, usage guidelines, and versioning.

steps.description: Audit the existing UI components and patterns to identify inconsistencies, duplicates, and gaps.

inputs.name: product-screens
inputs.desc: Screenshots or URLs of the current product screens

inputs.name: existing-component-list
inputs.desc: Any existing list of UI components in use

outputs.name: component-inventory
outputs.desc: Full inventory of UI components with usage frequency and inconsistencies

outputs.name: gap-analysis
outputs.desc: List of missing or inconsistent components that need standardization

process: Walk through each product screen and catalog every distinct UI component (buttons, inputs, cards, modals, navigation, typography).
Note where the same component appears in different styles or sizes across screens.
Identify components that are missing from the current set but needed based on the product's patterns.
Produce the component inventory with usage counts and the gap analysis.

steps.description: Define the design tokens (colors, typography, spacing, shadows, border radii) that form the foundation of the design system.

inputs.name: component-inventory
inputs.desc: The audited list of existing components

inputs.name: brand-guidelines
inputs.desc: Brand color palette, typography, and visual identity guidelines

outputs.name: token-specification
outputs.desc: Complete set of design tokens with names, values, and usage contexts

outputs.name: token-hierarchy
outputs.desc: The hierarchy of tokens (global, alias, component-specific)

process: Extract the color values, font families, sizes, spacing units, and shadow values currently in use.
Normalize them into a consistent scale (e.g., 4px spacing grid, type scale ratio).
Name each token using a semantic naming convention (e.g., color-primary, spacing-md, font-heading).
Define the token hierarchy: global tokens, alias tokens for themes, and component-specific overrides.
Produce the token specification document.

steps.description: Create the component library with standardized versions of each component based on the design tokens.

inputs.name: token-specification
inputs.desc: The design tokens to use as the foundation

inputs.name: gap-analysis
inputs.desc: Components that need to be created or standardized

outputs.name: component-library
outputs.desc: The complete set of standardized components with variants and states

outputs.name: component-specs
outputs.desc: Specification for each component (props, variants, states, accessibility)

process: For each component in the inventory and gap list, design the standardized version using the tokens.
Define the variants (size, color, state) and document the props and behavior.
Ensure each component meets accessibility requirements (contrast, focus states, ARIA labels).
Produce the component library and per-component specification sheets.

steps.description: Write the usage guidelines that explain when and how to use each component and token.

inputs.name: component-library
inputs.desc: The standardized components

inputs.name: component-specs
inputs.desc: The specification sheets for each component

outputs.name: usage-guidelines
outputs.desc: Documentation explaining when to use each component, with do/don't examples

outputs.name: pattern-recipes
outputs.desc: Common UI patterns built from the component library (forms, lists, dashboards)

process: For each component, write a usage section: what it is, when to use it, when not to use it, and examples.
Include do/don't pairs showing correct and incorrect usage.
Build pattern recipes for common page layouts using the components.
Produce the usage guidelines and pattern recipe documentation.

steps.description: Set up the versioning and change management process for the design system.

inputs.name: usage-guidelines
inputs.desc: The documented usage guidelines

inputs.name: component-library
inputs.desc: The component library to version

outputs.name: versioning-policy
outputs.desc: The versioning scheme, release process, and change log format

outputs.name: design-system-documentation
outputs.desc: The complete design system documentation package

process: Define the versioning scheme (semantic versioning for the system, per-component versioning).
Set up the change request process: how to propose, review, and approve changes to the system.
Define the release cadence and communication plan for updates.
Bundle everything into the design system documentation package.

description: Write and approve a creative brief from project intake through stakeholder review to final sign-off and team distribution.

steps.description: Gather the project context from the requestor including goals, audience, deliverables, timeline, and constraints.

inputs.name: project-request
inputs.desc: The initial project request or description from the requestor

inputs.name: requestor-context
inputs.desc: Who is requesting the work and their role

outputs.name: intake-summary
outputs.desc: Structured summary of goals, audience, deliverables, timeline, and constraints

outputs.name: clarification-log
outputs.desc: Questions asked and answers received during intake

process: Review the initial request and identify what information is missing.
Ask clarifying questions about goals (what success looks like), audience (who this is for), deliverables (what formats), timeline (key dates), and constraints (brand rules, platform limits).
Structure the answers into the intake summary.
Produce the intake summary and clarification log.

steps.description: Draft the creative brief from the intake summary.

inputs.name: intake-summary
inputs.desc: The structured intake information

inputs.name: brand-guidelines
inputs.desc: Brand voice, visual identity, and messaging guidelines

outputs.name: draft-brief
outputs.desc: The draft creative brief ready for stakeholder review

outputs.name: brief-assumptions
outputs.desc: Assumptions made during drafting that need validation

process: Write the brief sections: background, objective, target audience, key message, deliverables, timeline, and success metrics.
Reference the brand guidelines to set tone and visual direction.
Note any assumptions that need stakeholder validation.
Produce the draft brief and assumptions list.

steps.description: Route the draft brief for stakeholder review, collect feedback, and consolidate it.

inputs.name: draft-brief
inputs.desc: The draft creative brief

inputs.name: brief-assumptions
inputs.desc: Assumptions to validate with stakeholders

outputs.name: consolidated-feedback
outputs.desc: All stakeholder feedback organized by section

outputs.name: review-decisions
outputs.desc: Decisions made during review (approved assumptions, resolved conflicts)

process: Send the draft to each stakeholder with the assumptions list.
Collect feedback within the review window.
Consolidate and resolve conflicting feedback.
Produce the consolidated feedback and review decisions.

steps.description: Revise the brief based on feedback and get final sign-off.

inputs.name: draft-brief
inputs.desc: The original draft brief

inputs.name: consolidated-feedback
inputs.desc: The stakeholder feedback to incorporate

outputs.name: approved-brief
outputs.desc: The final approved creative brief

outputs.name: approval-record
outputs.desc: Who approved, when, and any conditions

process: Incorporate the feedback into the brief, updating each section.
Circulate the revised version for final approval.
Collect sign-offs and document any conditions or caveats.
Produce the approved brief and approval record.

steps.description: Distribute the approved brief to the creative team and kick off the project.

inputs.name: approved-brief
inputs.desc: The approved creative brief

inputs.name: approval-record
inputs.desc: The approval details and any conditions

outputs.name: team-assignments
outputs.desc: Who is responsible for each deliverable

outputs.name: project-kickoff-record
outputs.desc: Record of the kickoff including questions and clarifications from the team

process: Identify the team members needed for each deliverable.
Distribute the brief with role-specific context.
Hold the kickoff meeting to walk through the brief, answer questions, and confirm timelines.
Produce the team assignments and kickoff record.

description: Run a design review and approval cycle from submission through multi-stakeholder feedback to final sign-off.

steps.description: Prepare and submit the design for review with context and review criteria.

inputs.name: design-files
inputs.desc: The design deliverables to review (mockups, prototypes, specifications)

inputs.name: design-context
inputs.desc: The brief, requirements, and constraints the design was built against

outputs.name: review-package
outputs.desc: The design files with context, review criteria, and reviewer assignments

outputs.name: review-schedule
outputs.desc: The review timeline with deadlines for each reviewer

process: Package the design files with the original brief and requirements for context.
Define the review criteria (brand alignment, usability, technical feasibility, accessibility).
Assign reviewers by expertise (design lead, product, engineering, legal if needed).
Set the review deadline and produce the review package.

steps.description: Collect annotated feedback from each reviewer and consolidate it.

inputs.name: review-package
inputs.desc: The design package sent to reviewers

inputs.name: review-schedule
inputs.desc: The review timeline and deadlines

outputs.name: raw-feedback
outputs.desc: All reviewer comments, annotations, and scores organized by reviewer

outputs.name: conflict-flags
outputs.desc: Feedback items where reviewers disagree

process: Collect feedback from each reviewer within the deadline.
Organize comments by design area and severity (must-fix, should-fix, suggestion).
Identify conflicts where reviewers give opposing feedback.
Produce the raw feedback and conflict flags.

steps.description: Resolve conflicting feedback and prioritize the changes.

inputs.name: raw-feedback
inputs.desc: All collected feedback

inputs.name: conflict-flags
inputs.desc: Items where reviewers disagree

outputs.name: resolved-feedback
outputs.desc: The final list of changes to make, with priority and rationale

outputs.name: deferred-items
outputs.desc: Feedback items deferred to a future iteration with reasons

process: Walk through each conflict and make a decision (with the design lead or product owner).
Prioritize the remaining feedback by impact.
Identify items that can be deferred without blocking approval.
Produce the resolved feedback list and deferred items.

steps.description: Revise the design based on the resolved feedback.

inputs.name: design-files
inputs.desc: The original design files

inputs.name: resolved-feedback
inputs.desc: The prioritized list of changes

outputs.name: revised-design
outputs.desc: The updated design files incorporating the feedback

outputs.name: revision-notes
outputs.desc: Summary of what changed and why

process: Work through the resolved feedback list in priority order.
Make each change and note what was done and why.
Verify each change against the original review criteria.
Produce the revised design and revision notes.

steps.description: Get final approval on the revised design and produce the review record.

inputs.name: revised-design
inputs.desc: The revised design files

inputs.name: revision-notes
inputs.desc: Summary of changes made

outputs.name: approved-design
outputs.desc: The approved final design

outputs.name: design-review-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the review cycle (feedback, decisions, approvals)

process: Present the revised design to the approvers with the revision notes.
Collect final approval or identify remaining issues.
Archive the complete review record (original submission, feedback, revisions, approval).
Produce the approved design and review record.

description: Build and manage a brand asset library from inventory through organization, access control, and usage documentation.

steps.description: Inventory all brand assets across the organization.

inputs.name: asset-sources
inputs.desc: List of locations where brand assets are stored (drives, tools, repositories)

inputs.name: brand-guidelines
inputs.desc: Current brand guidelines to identify what counts as an official asset

outputs.name: asset-catalog
outputs.desc: Complete catalog of brand assets with type, location, version, and status

outputs.name: asset-issues
outputs.desc: Outdated, duplicate, or unauthorized assets found during inventory

process: Search each source location for brand assets (logos, icons, photos, templates, fonts, color files).
Catalog each asset with its type, format, dimensions, version, and current location.
Flag assets that are outdated, duplicated, or not aligned with current brand guidelines.
Produce the asset catalog and issues list.

steps.description: Organize the assets into a structured library with categories and metadata.

inputs.name: asset-catalog
inputs.desc: The complete catalog of brand assets

inputs.name: asset-issues
inputs.desc: Issues to resolve during organization

outputs.name: library-structure
outputs.desc: The folder structure, naming convention, and metadata schema

outputs.name: organized-library
outputs.desc: The assets organized into the library structure

process: Define the category structure (logos, photography, icons, templates, fonts, color palettes).
Set the naming convention and metadata fields (usage context, format, size, last updated).
Resolve the flagged issues (remove duplicates, archive outdated versions, flag unauthorized assets).
Produce the library structure and organized asset library.

steps.description: Set up access permissions and the request process for brand assets.

inputs.name: library-structure
inputs.desc: The organized library structure

inputs.name: team-roles
inputs.desc: The roles that need access (marketing, sales, partners, agencies)

outputs.name: access-policy
outputs.desc: Who can view, download, and use which assets

outputs.name: request-workflow
outputs.desc: The process for requesting new assets or custom versions

process: Define access levels by role (view-only, download, edit, admin).
Assign each asset category to the appropriate access levels.
Design the request workflow for assets not in the library or needing customization.
Produce the access policy and request workflow.

steps.description: Document the usage guidelines for each asset category.

inputs.name: organized-library
inputs.desc: The organized asset library

inputs.name: brand-guidelines
inputs.desc: Brand guidelines to reference

outputs.name: asset-usage-guide
outputs.desc: Usage rules for each asset category (clear space, minimum size, color versions, do/don't)

outputs.name: brand-asset-library-document
outputs.desc: The complete brand asset library setup document

process: For each asset category, write the usage rules (where to use, how to use, restrictions).
Include do/don't examples showing correct and incorrect usage.
Compile everything into the brand asset library setup document.
Produce the usage guide and complete library document.

description: Facilitate a five-day design sprint from challenge definition through prototyping and user testing.

steps.description: Define the sprint challenge, recruit the team, and prepare the materials.

inputs.name: business-problem
inputs.desc: The business problem or opportunity to address

inputs.name: available-team
inputs.desc: The people available to participate in the sprint

outputs.name: sprint-challenge
outputs.desc: The specific challenge statement the sprint will address

outputs.name: sprint-team
outputs.desc: The selected team members and their roles (decider, facilitator, experts)

process: Frame the business problem as a specific challenge question ('How might we...').
Select the sprint team: a decider (has authority), a facilitator, and domain experts.
Prepare the room, materials, and schedule for the five days.
Produce the challenge statement and team roster.

steps.description: Map the problem space and pick the target area for the sprint (day 1).

inputs.name: sprint-challenge
inputs.desc: The challenge statement

inputs.name: sprint-team
inputs.desc: The team members and their expertise

outputs.name: problem-map
outputs.desc: Visual map of the problem (user journey, actors, pain points)

outputs.name: sprint-target
outputs.desc: The specific part of the map the team will focus on

process: Have experts present what they know about the problem (customer data, business context, technical constraints).
Map the user journey from start to finish, noting pain points and opportunities.
Vote on which part of the map to target for the sprint.
Produce the problem map and selected target.

steps.description: Sketch solutions individually and decide on the best one (days 2-3).

inputs.name: problem-map
inputs.desc: The mapped problem space

inputs.name: sprint-target
inputs.desc: The target area to solve

outputs.name: winning-sketch
outputs.desc: The selected solution sketch with annotations

outputs.name: storyboard
outputs.desc: Step-by-step storyboard of the selected solution

process: Have each team member sketch their solution individually (no groupthink).
Present all sketches anonymously and vote on the strongest ideas.
The decider picks the winning solution or combines elements from multiple sketches.
Create a step-by-step storyboard of the winning solution.
Produce the winning sketch and storyboard.

steps.description: Build a realistic prototype of the solution (day 4).

inputs.name: storyboard
inputs.desc: The storyboard to turn into a prototype

inputs.name: sprint-target
inputs.desc: The target area for context on fidelity needed

outputs.name: prototype
outputs.desc: A realistic prototype ready for user testing

outputs.name: test-script
outputs.desc: The interview script and tasks for user testing

process: Assign prototype tasks to team members (screens, copy, data, assets).
Build the prototype at a fidelity level that users can react to (not pixel-perfect, but believable).
Write the test script with introduction, tasks, and follow-up questions.
Produce the prototype and test script.

steps.description: Test the prototype with users and produce the sprint report (day 5).

inputs.name: prototype
inputs.desc: The prototype to test

inputs.name: test-script
inputs.desc: The interview script and tasks

outputs.name: test-findings
outputs.desc: What worked, what did not, and patterns across test sessions

outputs.name: sprint-report
outputs.desc: Complete sprint report with challenge, solution, test results, and recommendations

process: Run 5 test sessions with target users using the test script.
Note what works, what confuses, and where users struggle.
Identify patterns across sessions (3+ users with the same reaction = a pattern).
Compile the sprint report: challenge, process, solution, test results, and next steps.
Produce the test findings and sprint report.

description: Manage a creative project from approved brief through production phases, approval gates, and final delivery.

steps.description: Scope the creative project from the approved brief, estimate the effort, and assign the team.

inputs.name: approved-brief
inputs.desc: The approved creative brief

inputs.name: team-availability
inputs.desc: Available team members and their current workload

outputs.name: project-plan
outputs.desc: Timeline, milestones, and deliverable schedule

outputs.name: team-assignments
outputs.desc: Who is responsible for each deliverable and phase

process: Break the brief into discrete deliverables and estimate the effort for each.
Assign team members based on skills and availability.
Build the project plan with milestones and review gates.
Produce the project plan and team assignments.

steps.description: Develop the initial creative concepts based on the brief.

inputs.name: approved-brief
inputs.desc: The creative brief to work from

inputs.name: team-assignments
inputs.desc: Who is developing the concepts

outputs.name: concept-options
outputs.desc: Two to three creative concept options with rationale

outputs.name: concept-recommendation
outputs.desc: The recommended concept with supporting reasoning

process: Research references and inspiration aligned with the brief's direction.
Develop two to three distinct concept options.
For each concept, explain how it meets the brief's objectives.
Recommend one concept and explain why.
Produce the concept options and recommendation.

steps.description: Execute the approved concept through draft, review, and revision cycles.

inputs.name: concept-options
inputs.desc: The concept options presented

inputs.name: project-plan
inputs.desc: The project timeline and milestones

outputs.name: production-deliverables
outputs.desc: The drafted deliverables ready for review

outputs.name: revision-log
outputs.desc: Record of revisions made during production

process: Produce the first draft of each deliverable based on the approved concept.
Run internal review with the creative lead.
Revise based on internal feedback.
Produce the deliverables and revision log.

steps.description: Run the stakeholder approval process for the produced deliverables.

inputs.name: production-deliverables
inputs.desc: The deliverables to approve

inputs.name: approved-brief
inputs.desc: The original brief for alignment check

outputs.name: approval-status
outputs.desc: Approved, approved with changes, or rejected with reasons

outputs.name: final-change-list
outputs.desc: Any remaining changes required before delivery

process: Present the deliverables to stakeholders alongside the original brief.
Collect approval decisions and any required changes.
If rejected, identify the specific misalignment and route back for revision.
Produce the approval status and final change list.

steps.description: Deliver the final creative assets and close out the project.

inputs.name: production-deliverables
inputs.desc: The approved deliverables

inputs.name: final-change-list
inputs.desc: Any last changes to apply

outputs.name: delivered-assets
outputs.desc: The final assets in all required formats and sizes

outputs.name: creative-project-record
outputs.desc: Complete project record (brief, concepts, revisions, approvals, final assets)

process: Apply any remaining changes from the final change list.
Export the assets in all required formats, sizes, and specifications.
Deliver the assets to the requestor with usage notes.
Archive the project record.
Produce the delivered assets and project record.

description: Plan and execute a photo shoot from creative direction through location scouting, shoot day management, and final asset delivery.

steps.description: Define the shot list and creative direction for the photo shoot.

inputs.name: shoot-brief
inputs.desc: The brief or purpose for the photo shoot

inputs.name: brand-guidelines
inputs.desc: Brand visual guidelines and mood references

outputs.name: shot-list
outputs.desc: Detailed list of shots with subject, composition, mood, and usage

outputs.name: creative-direction-doc
outputs.desc: Mood board, color palette, styling notes, and reference images

process: Define the purpose and usage of each photo (website, social, print, packaging).
Create the mood board with reference images, color palette, and styling direction.
Write the shot list with specifics for each shot (subject, angle, lighting, props).
Produce the shot list and creative direction document.

steps.description: Scout locations, hire crew, and plan the shoot logistics.

inputs.name: shot-list
inputs.desc: The shots to plan for

inputs.name: creative-direction-doc
inputs.desc: The creative direction to match locations and crew to

outputs.name: shoot-schedule
outputs.desc: The shoot day schedule (call times, locations, shot order, wrap)

outputs.name: crew-and-talent
outputs.desc: Hired crew and talent with roles, rates, and contact info

process: Scout and book locations that match the creative direction.
Hire the crew (photographer, assistant, stylist, hair/makeup) and talent (models).
Build the shoot day schedule with setup, shot order, and buffer time.
Produce the shoot schedule and crew/talent list.

steps.description: Manage the photo shoot day from setup through wrap.

inputs.name: shoot-schedule
inputs.desc: The planned schedule for the day

inputs.name: shot-list
inputs.desc: The shots to capture

outputs.name: raw-captures
outputs.desc: All captured images from the shoot

outputs.name: shoot-day-notes
outputs.desc: Notes on what went as planned, what changed, and any issues

process: Set up the location, lighting, and props per the creative direction.
Work through the shot list, checking each shot against the brief.
Adapt to on-set changes (weather, timing, talent availability).
Wrap the set and produce the raw captures and shoot day notes.

steps.description: Select the best images and retouch them to final quality.

inputs.name: raw-captures
inputs.desc: All images from the shoot

inputs.name: creative-direction-doc
inputs.desc: The visual direction to match during retouching

outputs.name: selected-images
outputs.desc: The curated set of best images with retouching applied

outputs.name: shoot-production-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the shoot (brief, direction, logistics, selects, finals)

process: Cull the raw images to the best options for each shot on the list.
Present selects to the creative lead for approval.
Retouch the approved selects (color correction, cropping, cleanup).
Export in all required formats and sizes.
Produce the selected images and shoot production record.

description: Design product packaging from specifications gathering through concept development, print-ready artwork, and press proofing.

steps.description: Gather the product specifications and regulatory requirements for the packaging.

inputs.name: product-info
inputs.desc: Product name, dimensions, weight, and materials

inputs.name: regulatory-context
inputs.desc: Industry regulations and labeling requirements (FDA, FTC, local laws)

outputs.name: packaging-specs
outputs.desc: Complete specifications (dimensions, materials, print area, die line)

outputs.name: mandatory-elements
outputs.desc: Required text, symbols, and disclosures for the packaging

process: Document the product dimensions, weight, and packaging material.
Identify the print area, die line, and fold/glue zones.
List all mandatory labeling elements (ingredients, warnings, barcodes, recycling symbols).
Produce the packaging specs and mandatory elements list.

steps.description: Develop packaging design concepts based on the specs and brand guidelines.

inputs.name: packaging-specs
inputs.desc: The physical specifications and constraints

inputs.name: brand-guidelines
inputs.desc: Brand visual identity and design guidelines

outputs.name: concept-mockups
outputs.desc: Two to three packaging concept mockups with rationale

outputs.name: selected-concept
outputs.desc: The chosen concept with stakeholder approval

process: Research competitor packaging and category conventions.
Design two to three concepts that meet the specs and align with the brand.
Create 3D mockups for each concept to show how they look on shelf.
Present to stakeholders and select the final concept.
Produce the concept mockups and selected concept.

steps.description: Prepare the print-ready artwork from the selected concept.

inputs.name: selected-concept
inputs.desc: The approved packaging concept

inputs.name: mandatory-elements
inputs.desc: Required text and symbols to include

outputs.name: print-ready-files
outputs.desc: Production-ready artwork files (correct color mode, bleeds, dieline, separations)

outputs.name: preflight-report
outputs.desc: Preflight check results (fonts, images, colors, bleeds)

process: Build the final artwork on the die line template in the correct color mode (CMYK or spot).
Place all mandatory elements (text, barcodes, symbols) in the required positions.
Run the preflight check (resolution, fonts, bleeds, color separations).
Produce the print-ready files and preflight report.

steps.description: Coordinate the proof approval and press check with the printer.

inputs.name: print-ready-files
inputs.desc: The production-ready artwork

inputs.name: packaging-specs
inputs.desc: The physical specs for the printer

outputs.name: approved-proof
outputs.desc: The approved proof with sign-off

outputs.name: packaging-design-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the packaging design (specs, concepts, artwork, proof)

process: Send the print-ready files to the printer with the specs.
Review the proof for color accuracy, registration, and text correctness.
Approve the proof or request corrections.
Attend the press check if color accuracy is critical.
Produce the approved proof and packaging design record.

description: Localize content for multiple markets from string extraction through translation, in-market review, and integration testing.

steps.description: Identify and extract the content to localize.

inputs.name: source-content
inputs.desc: The original content to localize (UI strings, marketing copy, documentation)

inputs.name: target-locales
inputs.desc: The markets and languages to localize for

outputs.name: content-inventory
outputs.desc: All localizable strings and assets with their context

outputs.name: localization-scope
outputs.desc: Total word count, asset count, and estimated effort per locale

process: Walk through the source content and extract every user-facing string.
Tag each string with context (where it appears, character limits, tone requirements).
Identify non-text assets that need localization (images with text, videos, PDFs).
Calculate the scope per locale and produce the content inventory.

steps.description: Translate and culturally adapt the content for each target locale.

inputs.name: content-inventory
inputs.desc: The strings and assets to translate

inputs.name: target-locales
inputs.desc: The locales to translate for

outputs.name: translated-content
outputs.desc: Translated strings and adapted assets for each locale

outputs.name: adaptation-notes
outputs.desc: Cultural adaptations made and their reasoning

process: Translate each string with context, not word-for-word.
Adapt cultural references, idioms, date/number formats, and imagery for each locale.
Flag items that cannot be directly translated and propose alternatives.
Produce the translated content and adaptation notes.

steps.description: Have in-market reviewers check the translations for accuracy and naturalness.

inputs.name: translated-content
inputs.desc: The translations to review

inputs.name: adaptation-notes
inputs.desc: Notes on cultural adaptations for reviewer context

outputs.name: reviewed-content
outputs.desc: Translations with reviewer corrections incorporated

outputs.name: review-feedback
outputs.desc: Reviewer comments and corrections per locale

process: Send translated content to native-speaking reviewers in each target market.
Collect feedback on accuracy, naturalness, tone, and cultural fit.
Incorporate corrections and flag any remaining disputes.
Produce the reviewed content and review feedback.

steps.description: Integrate the localized content and test it in context.

inputs.name: reviewed-content
inputs.desc: The reviewed and corrected translations

inputs.name: source-content
inputs.desc: The original content for comparison

outputs.name: integrated-content
outputs.desc: The localized content integrated into the product or platform

outputs.name: localization-record
outputs.desc: Complete localization record (scope, translations, reviews, testing)

process: Import the translated strings into the product or CMS.
Test each locale for text overflow, truncation, layout breaks, and encoding issues.
Verify links, images, and dynamic content in each locale.
Produce the integrated content and localization record.

description: Conduct a UX audit from scope definition through heuristic evaluation, competitor benchmarking, and prioritized fix recommendations.

steps.description: Define the audit scope, select the heuristics, and set up the evaluation framework.

inputs.name: product-to-audit
inputs.desc: The product, app, or website to audit

inputs.name: audit-goals
inputs.desc: What the audit should focus on (onboarding, checkout, navigation, accessibility)

outputs.name: audit-plan
outputs.desc: The scope, heuristics, user flows to evaluate, and evaluation criteria

outputs.name: competitor-list
outputs.desc: Competitors to benchmark against

process: Define which parts of the product to audit based on the goals.
Select the evaluation heuristics (Nielsen's 10, WCAG, custom criteria).
Identify the key user flows to walk through.
Select two to three competitors for benchmarking.
Produce the audit plan and competitor list.

steps.description: Walk through the key user flows and document usability issues.

inputs.name: audit-plan
inputs.desc: The scope and heuristics to evaluate against

inputs.name: product-to-audit
inputs.desc: The product to evaluate

outputs.name: issue-list
outputs.desc: All usability issues found with severity rating, heuristic violated, and screenshot

outputs.name: flow-annotations
outputs.desc: Annotated screenshots of each user flow showing the issues

process: Walk through each user flow as a first-time user and as a returning user.
At each step, evaluate against the selected heuristics.
Document each issue with a description, severity (critical, major, minor, cosmetic), the heuristic violated, and a screenshot.
Produce the issue list and annotated flow screenshots.

steps.description: Benchmark the product against competitors on the same user flows.

inputs.name: competitor-list
inputs.desc: The competitors to benchmark against

inputs.name: audit-plan
inputs.desc: The user flows and criteria to compare on

outputs.name: benchmark-comparison
outputs.desc: Side-by-side comparison of the product vs competitors on each flow

outputs.name: competitive-gaps
outputs.desc: Areas where competitors do better and what can be learned

process: Walk through the same user flows on each competitor product.
Score each product on the evaluation criteria.
Identify where the audited product falls behind and where it leads.
Produce the benchmark comparison and competitive gaps.

steps.description: Prioritize the usability fixes by impact and effort.

inputs.name: issue-list
inputs.desc: All issues found during the audit

inputs.name: competitive-gaps
inputs.desc: Areas where competitors are ahead

outputs.name: prioritized-fixes
outputs.desc: Issues ranked by priority with estimated effort and expected impact

outputs.name: ux-audit-report
outputs.desc: Complete audit report (scope, findings, benchmarks, recommendations)

process: Score each issue on impact (how many users affected, how badly) and effort (design + dev time).
Rank by impact-to-effort ratio: high impact, low effort fixes first.
Group into quick wins, planned improvements, and long-term investments.
Compile the full audit report with executive summary, findings, benchmarks, and prioritized recommendations.
Produce the prioritized fixes and audit report.
